## Goal

Provide one command-line entry point that launches the game with either terminal or Pygame rendering.

## Files

- `gridworld/__main__.py`

## Tasks

- Complete the supplied entry-point script, integrating the models, engine and components from S0-02, S0-03 and S0-04.
- Use the existing `--render` argument to select `terminal` or `pygame`, with `terminal` as the default. Preserve the existing `--level` argument, which defaults to `levels/n0.json`.
- Load the level and create the selected renderer, its input source, the controller and the engine.
- For terminal mode, use `BashRender` and `TerminalInput`. For Pygame mode, use the supplied `PygameRender` and `PygameInput(renderer)` without changing their implementations.
- Start the renderer before running the engine and ensure cleanup with `finally`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both launch commands shown below work from the repository root.
- [ ] Omitting `--render` selects terminal mode. `--help` documents the available choices, and an unsupported value is rejected before the game starts.
- [ ] The launcher loads the map selected by `--level`, using `levels/n0.json` by default.
- [ ] Both modes inject their input source into `Controller` and pass the level, controller and renderer to `Engine`.
- [ ] Pygame uses `PygameInput(renderer)` and `Controller(input_source)`; Pygame calls remain on the main thread.
- [ ] The renderer starts before the game loop and is closed when the loop ends, including if the loop raises an exception.
- [ ] Both modes produce the same positions, turn counts and victory for the S0-03 acceptance route, without changing Engine's rules.
- [ ] The Pygame window stays responsive without input and after victory. Escape or the window close button closes Pygame; `:quit` closes the terminal game.

```sh
uv run python -m gridworld --render terminal
uv run python -m gridworld --render pygame
```

## Evidence

Attach a victory screenshot and the commands used to a reviewed PR linked to this issue. At the start of S1, demonstrate the full S0-03 acceptance route and clean shutdown in both modes, plus the default mode, help output and rejection of an unsupported renderer. Explain how the launcher assembles the same engine with different input and rendering components.

Use manual checks in S0. Automated tests begin in S1.
Organize the work and peer reviews within your group.
